skill.name: nx-workspace
skill.description: Explore Nx workspaces, inspect resolved project configuration, analyze targets and dependencies, identify affected projects, and troubleshoot task configuration failures.
skill.summary: Inspect Nx projects, targets, dependencies, affected sets, and workspace configuration through structured CLI output.
skill.author: nrwl

security_audit.summary: All 47 external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples, not Ruby or shell command substitution. Both sensitive-file findings are jq `.key` projections, not certificate or private-key access. Semantic review found that `nx sync` and `nx reset` can alter workspace or cache state despite the read-only claim.

remediation.issue: The read-only claim conflicts with state-changing troubleshooting commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove nx sync and nx reset, or label them as optional commands requiring explicit approval after reviewing pending changes.

semantic_findings.title: Read-only Claim Conflicts With State-changing Commands
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares read-only exploration, then recommends nx sync and nx reset. These commands can change workspace files or clear local Nx state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The contradiction is explicit. Nx sync and nx reset are operational commands rather than read-only inspection.

content.value_statement: Nx monorepos hide resolved targets, dependencies, and affected projects behind layered configuration. This skill uses Nx JSON output and command-line filters to produce precise workspace answers.
actual_capabilities: Lists and filters projects by name, glob, tag, type, target, or affected status.
Retrieves resolved project configuration and inspects target executors, options, inputs, and outputs.
Reads workspace settings from nx.json and points to installed Nx configuration schemas.
Analyzes the project graph to identify dependencies and dependents.
Investigates missing targets and stale workspace state with focused Nx commands.
Finds projects affected by branches, commits, uncommitted changes, or untracked files.
limitations: Requires Nx through a global install or the workspace package manager.
Structured filtering examples require jq or an equivalent local JSON tool.
Nx commands load installed workspace dependencies and should run only in trusted repositories.
The suggested nx sync and nx reset commands can modify files or local cache state.

use_cases.title: Map an unfamiliar monorepo
use_cases.description: List applications and libraries, inspect their tags, and trace dependencies before making a change.

use_cases.title: Audit target configuration
use_cases.description: Compare resolved build, test, and lint targets across projects without relying on partial project files.

use_cases.title: Scope continuous integration
use_cases.description: Identify affected projects for a branch or commit range and confirm each required target exists.

prompt_templates.title: List workspace projects
prompt_templates.prompt: List every project in this Nx workspace. Group applications and libraries, then note each project with a build target.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect one project
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the resolved configuration for [project]. Summarize its root, tags, targets, executors, inputs, and outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Trace dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Show what [project] depends on and which projects depend on it. Use the Nx project graph and summarize dependency types.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an affected target
prompt_templates.prompt: Find projects affected between [base] and [head]. Verify their [target] configuration and explain any missing or inconsistent targets.

output_examples.input: List applications and show which ones provide a build target.
output_examples.output: Applications: storefront, admin, and api. storefront and admin provide build targets; api exposes serve and test only.
Direct dependents: storefront and admin. No other project has a direct dependency on shared-ui.

output_examples.input: Why does api:lint fail with missing configuration?
output_examples.output: The resolved api configuration has build, serve, and test targets, but no lint target. Add or infer lint configuration before running api:lint.

best_practices: Use Nx JSON output for project, target, and graph questions.
Inspect resolved project configuration instead of relying only on project.json.
Review repository trust and pending changes before running any state-changing command.
anti_patterns: Do not count or parse complex terminal output manually when structured output exists.
Do not assume every project exposes standard build, test, or lint targets.
Do not run nx sync or nx reset as read-only diagnostics without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill change source files?
faq.answer: Most exploration commands are read-only. The documented nx sync command can update workspace files, so review and approve it separately.

faq.question: Does it require a global Nx installation?
faq.answer: No. It can use npx, pnpx, or yarn according to the workspace package manager and lockfile.

faq.question: Why inspect resolved project configuration?
faq.answer: Nx plugins can infer targets that project.json does not contain. The resolved configuration includes those inferred targets.

faq.question: Can it find affected projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports automatic bases, explicit branches, commit ranges, uncommitted changes, and untracked files.

faq.question: Can it explain project dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses printed project graph data to identify dependencies and reverse dependents.

faq.question: What tools improve structured analysis?
faq.answer: Nx JSON output is primary. jq supports filtering, selection, counting, and extraction from that output.
